FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Methods of Test for Petroleum, Petroluem Products and Lubricants Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. This Indian Standard aligns with ASTM D 2534-88 `Non-condensable hydrocarbon products by Gas Chromatography' issued by American Materials ( USA ). gases in C2 and lighter Society for Testing and

In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`.

METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS
IP:1441 NON-CONDENSABLE GASES IN C2 AND LIGHTER HYDROCARBON PRODUCTS ~Y-GAs CHROMATOGRAPHY 1 SCOPE 1.1. This testmethod covers the determination of hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen and carbon monoxide in the parts per million volume ( ppmv ) range in C2 and lighter hydrocarbon porducts. This test method should be applicable to light hydrocarbons other than ethylene, but the test programme did not include them. 1.2 This standard may involve hazardous materials, operations, and equipment. This standard does not purport to address all of the safety problems associated with its use. It is the responsibility of the user of this standard to establish appropriate safety and health practices and determine the applicability of regulatory limitations prior to use. 2 SUMMARY OF TEST METHOD 4.2 Detectors Thermal Conductivity

If a methanation reactor is used, a flame ionization detector is also required. To determine carbon monoxide with a flame ionization detector, a methanation reactor must be inserted between the column and the detector and hydrogen added as a reduction gas. Details on the preparation and use of the reactor are given in Annex A. 4.3 Constant Volume Gas Sampling Valve 4.4 Column Any column or set of columns that are capable of resolving the components listed in the scope can be used. Copper, stainless steel, or aluminium tubing may be used. The columns chosen must afford a resolution such that the depth of the valleys ahead of the trace peak is no less than 50 percent of the trace peak height. 4.5 Recorder A recorder with a full-scale second or less and a maximum f 0.3 percent of full scale. 4.6 Oven The oven used for activating molecular sieve must be maintained at 260 to 288�C ( 500 to 550�F ) and should be designed so that the gases may be displaced continuously by a stream of inert gas. The oven may be thermostated piece of l-in pipe about 0.3 m ( 1 ft ) in length. Electrical heating tapes or other means may be used for heating provided the heat is distributed uniformly.
NOTE - The use of copper tubing is not recommended with samples containing acetylene as this cor~ld lead to the formatio;] of potentially explosive copper acetylide.

The sample is separated in a gas-solid chromatographic system using molecular sieves as the solid adsorbent. The concentration of the gases to be determined is calculated from the Argon recorded peak heights or peak areas. can be used as a carrier gas for the determination of hydrozen in concentrations below 100 ppmv. Argon, if present in the sample, interferes with oxygen determination. 3 SIGNIFICANCE AND USE

response of 2 rate of noise of

The presence of trace amounts of hydrogen oxygen and carbon monoxide can have deleterious effect in certain processes using hydrocarbon products as feed stock. This test method is suitable for setting specifications, for use as an internal quality control tool and for use in development and research work. 4 APPARATUS 4.1 Chromatograph Any chromatographic instrument having either a thermal conductivity or ionization detector with an overall sensitivity sufficient to detect 2 ppmv or less of the compounds listed in the scope, with a peak height of at least 2 mm without loss of resolution. 1

5.3 Gases for Calibration Pure or research grade hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon monoxide will be needed to prepare synthetic standard samples as described in this test method. ( Warning -. see Notes ). Certified calibration blends are commercially available from numerous sources and can be used as the synthetic standard samples.
NOTES
1 Warning - Flammable gases, hazardous pressure ( see also B-1 to B-5 ). 2 Warning - Flammable. Poison Harmful if inhaled. Dangerous when exposed to flame ( see also B-5 ). 3 Warnirg - Hazardous pressure ( see aIso B-2 ).

8.2 Prepare at least three synthetic standard samples (see Annex C) containing the compounds to be determined over the range of concentration desired in the products to be analysed, using the pure gases or the certified blend, for the preparation of the second, third and following calibration samples it is always preferable not to dilute the first sample. 8.3 Inject a known volume of one of the standard samples, using a minimum of 1 ml for detecting 2 ppmv.
NOTE - Use of reverse-flow arrangement will facilitate removal of heavier gases and decrease the elapsed time of analysis.

APPARATUS

Column Packing

Crush in a porcelain mortar and seive to 40 to 60-mesh size about 200 g of molecular sieves 5A in order to have enough for several columns. A]] work of preparing molecular sieves and packing columns with this material shall be done rapidly, preferably under a blanket of dry nitrogen in order to minimize moisture absorption. Heat the screened molecular sieves in an oven at 274 f 14�C ( 525 f 25�F ) for 24 hours purging with dry nitrogen at a rate of about 5 ml/min during this time. The nitrogen rate is not critical and can be measured by any convenient means such as an orifice meter, rotameter, manometer, etc. Do not use a wet test meter. 7.2 Chromatographic
Column

8.5 Prepare a chart for each compound, plotting the peak height of the compound or peak area of the compound against the concentration of the compounds in ppmv. The peak area can be determined by any method that meets the precision requirements of Section 11 Methods found to be acceptable include planimetering, integration ( electronic or mechanical or computer processing ), and triangulation. 9 PROCEDURE
9.1 Connect

the sample cylinder containing a gaseous sample to the gas sample valve with a metal tube and allow the sample to flow from the sample tube for about l/2 min at a rate of 70 to 100 ml/min. 9.2 inject into the instrument the same volume of sample as used for calibration ( pressure of sample and calibration gas must be the same in the sample loop ) and record the peak areas or peak heights desired.

11.1.2 Reproducibility

11.1 The precision of this test method as determined by statistical examination of interlaboratory results is as follows.

The difference between two single and independent results obtained by different operators working in different laboratories on identical test material wouId, in long run, and in the normal and correct operation of the test method, exceed the following values only in one case in twenty:

11.1.1 Repeatability The difference between successive test results, obtained by the same operator with the same apparatus under constant operating conditions on identical test material would, in long run, and in the normal and correct operation of the test method, exceed the following values only in one case in twenty:

NOTE - It is believed that the methods for oxygen and nitrogen are better than the precision would indicate, and that the poor reproducibility is attributable to the difficulty of excluding air frcm these samples. Precise results are heavily dependent upon extreme care in sampling and handling. The use of continuous analyzers is preferred, and is recommended whenever circumstances permit.

ANNEX A
NON-MANDATORY A-O PREPARATION REACTOR A-l GENERAL OF METHANATION INFORMATION solution over the chromosorb. Warm the mixture to 65�C on a hot plate and evaporate the methanol with constant stirring, until the mixture appears dry. The resultant catalyst is subsequently reduced in the hydrogenation tube during instrument preparation. A-6 PROCEDURE A-6.1 Using glass ~vool as a retainer, pack the 152-4 mm ( 6-in ) bv 6.35 m ( l/4-in ) stainless tube 38.1 mm ( 1*5-`in ) from either end with catalyst. Allowing 38.1 mm ( l-5-in ) of space at each end of the tube ensures failure to produce a highly toxic compound, nickel carbonyl. A-6.2 The aluminium block should have three holes drilled in it. One hole should be drilled through the block lengthwise, in the centre of the end, 6.35 mm ( l/4-in ) in diameter. Anothe;. hole should be drilled on either side of the ccntre. Its dimensions should be 50.X by 9.53 mm ( 2-in by 0.375-in ) in diameter. This hsle will accept the cartridge heater. The third hole should be 50.8 mm ( 2-in ) long and 3.18 mm ( l/&in ) in diameter and on the opposite side of centre as the cartridge heater. This will accept the thermocouple sensor. 6.3 Place the packed tube through the block so that the ends extend equally from either end of the block. Place the cartridge heater in the block, wrap the system with insulation and place the thermocouple in 3.18 mm ( l/S-in ) hole. Use only stainless steel connectors and attach one end of the 6.35 mm ( l/4-in ) packed tube to detector inlet. Attach the discharge end of the chromatographic column to the other end of the reactor through a tee connector. The tee is provided in order to introduce 30 ml/min of hydrogen to the methanator. A-6.4 After setting the hydrogen flow, connect the heater to a variable auto transformer. The setting should be approximately 55. Allow the catalyst to condition for 24 h at 300�C. Normal operating temperature for the methanator should be 325 f 25�C.

This method describes the preparation of a methanation reactor to convert carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide to methane, which can then be determined using a flame ionization detector at levels less than 1 ppm. A-2 SIGNIFICANCE AND USE

The use of a flame ionization detector to enhance the detection limits for carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide is made possible by conversion of these gases to methane. A-3 APPARATUS A-3.1 Tubing -152.4 mm ( l/4-in ) stainless steel. ( 6-in ) or 6.35 mm by to

C-l An example of a satisfactory concentrate may be as follows: .Constituents Percent 10 Carbon dioxide ( CO, ) 45 Methane ( CH, ) Ethane ( C,HB ) 25 Propylene ( C,H, ) 20 The concentrate can be prepared using the gas blending manifold as shown in Fig. 2 or using a similar apparatus as follows:

Evacuate the apparatus and add the component in the order of increasing vapour pressure that is, propylene, carbon dioxide, ethane and methane. Record the increase in pressure on the manometer as each component is added. Close the reservoir and evacuate the manometer after each addition. A certified calibration blend can be obtained and also be used as the concentrate.
